_about: The fire country (Mount Ember, Hearthold, the forge, Cinder Springs, Cinderwick, the Ash Coast) as a plan (Claude D, lane D, 21 Oct), in Claude F's region-plan schema (scripts/art/region_plan.py, #174), written by scripts/art/regions/sunstone_plan.py from the brief docs/vision/regions/sunstone-basin-fire-country.md (v5.3) and lane G's routes. World px on the 11264 x 6912 canvas. Tiers are lane G's absolute world tiers (base_tier 0), outlines in screen space on the 8 px grid in straight runs (the painter rounds the corners: eastward-edges 1.5); a tier is a 32 px south face, west and east ends are side bands. Resolution-independent: the art density (about 2x, pending Matt's verdict) does not move anything here.

faces._about: Each biome draws its own edges (to-all-reuse-rule) on the shared grammar (eastward-edges.md). The cliff core's canyon set (#165) is 40 px; these plans keep lane G's 32 px tier, so the canyon set needs a 32 px face or the tier map is read at 40 (asked of Claude A).

ground._about: Ground kinds by place, for the painter, in the dry kit's terms (#137) on the house ramps per terrain (house-style.md): big calm fields of one tone with a few large soft blotches, tufts and stones clumped by rule, never speckle (to-all-clean).
ground.steppe: short yellowing grass in wide fields, bunchgrass clumps, the odd single tree, drystone folds
ground.rift: banded ochre and red gorge walls; the green strip's meadow and willows in the bays and at the confluences
ground.scrub: hardpan and gravel with sage and creosote in clumps, saguaro and barrel cacti alone, mesas on the skyline
ground.oasis: date palms over a stone-rimmed pool, orchards on channels, reeds, the water-seller's awning
ground.gulch: packed dust street, boardwalks, false fronts, orchards along the Amber, the platform's cinders
ground.lode: spoil and rubble on a bench under the massif face, timber props, ore tubs on a rail stub
ground.canyon: a gravel floor and the Amber's wash between red and buff walls in bands; shade, boulders at the feet
ground.salt-lake: a white salt pan with polygon crust, a pale shore of gravel, bleached snags
ground.dunes: low dunes and tussocks thickening west into the dune wall with thorn scrub
ground.ash: grey ash over the scrub thinning north (dithered nowhere: blotches), drifts, fireweed, basalt stumps
ground.flows: the old flow: crusted rubble grown over with fireweed and lava-stone scrub; the young flow: black crust with glowing seams, steaming at the toe
ground.hearthold: castle stone streets in steps, the curtain wall, the keep on its crag
ground.forge: basalt yard on the caldera lip, coal heaps, the crater's glow behind the rim
ground.springs: stone-rimmed hot pools in terraces, warm wet basalt, ferns in the steam
ground.cinderwick: black sand, nets on poles, charcoal clamps, a few huts above the cove
ground.coast: the green windward shelf: meadow and coastal woods, then snags among fireweed in the dead forest; black sand below the flows

notes: The routes' long straight runs (up to 416 px on the Drover's Road) follow Matt's grid ruling (21 Oct 11:44, to-all-grid-2x); region_plan.py's check 16 (240 px) predates it.
The brief puts the desert line's viaduct 'upstream' of Drover's bridge but at (4290, 3720), downstream; the plan keeps the coordinates.

The fire country: v5.3 4.7 is followed (the chasm bridge crosses the old flow from the summit's south-west breach; the crust causeway the young flow from the south-east vent); table 5.2's 'young west flow' is read as that.
Hearthold's stepped streets are laid as six terraces (9 to 13) with the routes' stairs and lane D's streets; the brief's 24 stairs come with the castle kit.
Set pieces of the ash biome wait for its edge set in the cliff core (not built yet).
